Hi all — follow-up and technical recap from today’s deep-dive. I’ve summarized the sizing assumptions, recommended topology, and operational controls below. See attached sizing workbook and architecture diagram for the numbers and drawings.

Summary of customer targets we validated:
- User-facing P95 target: 150ms for core conversational flows; 500ms for background jobs.
- Sustained throughput target: 200 req/s with peaks to 400 req/s for short bursts.
- Model profile: 13B dense transformer, sequence length up to 1024, median prompt+response tokens ~320, high context reuse per session.

Sizing assumptions and recommendation:
- Model precision: recommend 8-bit quantization (Q8) as the default for production; 4-bit (Q4) could be possible but requires additional QA for quality regressions. Q8 gives ~1.8x memory reduction vs FP16 with negligible latency hit in our runtime.
- Hardware footprint: for US-west deployment we recommend a dedicated pool of 6 x A100-40GB (or equivalent) for baseline workloads. This maps to sustained 200 req/s with p95 ~120–170ms depending on batching. Leave 2 node buffer for autoscale headroom (recommended pool target: 8 nodes).
- Batching strategy: micro-batching window 8–12ms for interactive flows and adaptive batching for background jobs. Maintain a max batch size of 32 for safety.
- KV cache: enable session-level KV cache with a 30m TTL for short-lived sessions; cache sharding aligned with pod affinity to reduce cross-pod fetches. Expected cache hit rates ~60–75% given high context reuse, which reduces token generation count and improves latency.
- Autoscaling & fallback: scale-up policy based on queue length and sustained CPU/GPU utilization; fast-burst buffer via a lower-cost hosted fallback model (redwood-hosted-small) to absorb excess 30–40% of burst traffic with graceful degradation of QoE.

Networking & security checklist:
- VPC peering + private routes; customer-managed KMS with envelope encryption; TLS in transit and mutual TLS for control plane hooks.
- Audit logging: retain request metadata and token/usage aggregates for 1 year (no raw prompt storage unless agreed).

Operational considerations:
- Canary rollout plan (10% → 50% → 100%) with perf regressions gated by a small prompt eval set.
- Regression monitoring: continuous evals on prompt set and alerting for >3% generation-quality regressions or >10% latency regressions at p95.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx, arch-diagram.png, redwood-sla-data-sheet.pdf

- Marissa to route procurement contacts for contract and KMS onboarding.
